value.body: A medical representative visits doctors, hospitals and chemists in an assigned territory to explain a pharmaceutical company's medicines and track prescriptions and stock. Employers are mainly pharma companies and their marketing divisions. A typical day is clinic and chemist calls in the morning and evening, with reporting and planning in between.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Pharm or a B.Sc in life sciences
items.note: Some companies also hire other graduates

items.label: Rules on promotion
items.value: Uniform Code for Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices (UCPMP), 2024
items.note: Limits gifts, travel and sponsorship for doctors

items.label: Indian pharma market
items.note: ~US$23.5 bn domestic consumption and ~US$26.5 bn exports

value.title: How you get in
value.body: After graduation, freshers apply to pharma companies' field-force openings and usually join as trainee representatives after a short product and selling training. A two-wheeler, a driving licence and the local language are often expected.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Explaining a drug's uses, doses and side effects clearly
Planning daily doctor and chemist visits across a territory
Logging calls and orders in a field-reporting app
Tracking stock and sales at chemists in the area
Following up on objections and queries

value.title: At a glance
items: A common progression is Area Sales Manager, then Regional Manager; some move into product management or sales training.
Pay often includes target-linked incentives, so earnings can vary month to month.
Daily travel within the territory and occasional transfers are part of the job.

value.title: B.Pharm enrolment, regular mode
value.note: Regular mode only. Based on institutions that responded to the survey; part of the year-to-year change reflects response coverage.

competition.note: BBA graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
